description: One slow or lost item at the front of a queue delays everything behind it: whole responses in HTTP/1.1, lost TCP packets in HTTP/2.
Many requests travel at once over one TCP connection as interleaved frames of numbered streams, with compressed headers.
The UDP-based transport under HTTP/3: independent streams, a combined transport and TLS handshake, and connections that survive a network change.
A schema-first RPC framework on HTTP/2: the schema generates typed clients and servers and messages travel in a compact binary format.
A long-lived HTTP response of type `text/event-stream` carrying server-to-client events, with automatic reconnection and `Last-Event-ID` resumption.
A full-duplex connection opened by an HTTP upgrade (`101 Switching Protocols` on HTTP/1.1) where both sides send frames at any time.
The server holds a request open until there is data or a timeout, then the client immediately asks again.
